content.title: About
content.content: Farm raised catfish is a fresh fish harvested from controlled aquaculture systems. It has firm white flesh, a mild sweet flavor, and a dense texture. Raw catfish is commonly used in sushi, ceviche, and as a base for marinades.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Catfish belong to the order Siluriformes and are closely related to other freshwater species.
Farmed catfish are raised in closed recirculating systems, allowing precise control of water quality and feed.
Raw catfish is rich in omega‑3 fatty acids, which support cardiovascular health.
Compared with wild-caught fish, farmed catfish typically has lower levels of environmental contaminants.
Catfish is a staple in many cuisines, from Southern United States dishes to Asian preparations.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Omega‑3 fatty acids help lower triglycerides and support heart health.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: Catfish provides easily digestible protein essential for muscle building and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: Catfish supplies selenium, phosphorus, and potassium, beneficial for immunity and bone health.

items.title: Low mercury
items.content: Unlike large predatory fish, catfish has minimal mercury accumulation.

items.title: Foodborne infection risk
items.content: Raw fish can harbor parasites and bacteria; only use certified products and follow strict hygiene.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Farmed catfish may be brined; people with hypertension should monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large portions of raw fish can cause gastrointestinal upset in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice raw catfish thinly for sushi or sashimi, or prepare it in ceviche with lime juice, cilantro, and chili. It can also be marinated in soy sauce with ginger. Serve with fresh lemon or lime wedges.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep catfish refrigerated at 0‑2 °C in an airtight container for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C using vacuum‑sealed packaging. Before consumption, check for a fresh, mild scent; discard if it smells sour or ammonia‑like.
